title: Stroke: history or residual deficits
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's past stroke and any residual deficits.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for residual right-sided hemiparesis.

HPI
The patient is an 86-year-old male presenting today for a scheduled follow-up regarding his chronic condition following a prior ischemic stroke. He reports that his functional status remains stable. He continues to experience right-sided hemiparesis, which he manages daily. He notes that he is left-handed and continues to perform most activities of daily living using his left side. He denies any recent falls or significant changes in his mobility. He is seeking a review of his current physical status and medication management.

Medication List
1. Lisinopril 10mg daily
2. Atorvastatin 40mg daily
3. Aspirin 81mg daily

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 132/78 mmHg
Heart Rate: 72 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Temperature: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on room air
Weight: 175 lbs

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 6.2%
eGFR: 65 mL/min/1.73m2
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L
LDL: 88 mg/dL

Review of Systems
The patient reports no chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. He denies any recent headaches, dizziness, or vision changes. He reports no joint pain or significant fatigue. He denies any changes in bowel or bladder function.

Social History
The patient resides in his private residence with his wife. He retired five years ago and enjoys gardening and listening to music. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally in small amounts.

Family History
Father: Deceased, history of hypertension.
Mother: Deceased, history of type 2 diabetes.
Siblings: One brother, history of coronary artery disease.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. He is cooperative and pleasant. Physical exam reveals a lean, well-nourished male. Neurological exam shows persistent right-sided hemiparesis with diminished motor strength in the right upper and lower extremities. He demonstrates clear left-hand dominant movement during the evaluation. Reflexes are symmetric. Sensation is intact to light touch throughout.

Assessment
1. Residual right-sided hemiparesis following a history of ischemic stroke.
2. Hypertension.
3. Hyperlipidemia.

Plan
1. Continue current medications as prescribed.
2. Encouraged continued physical therapy exercises to maintain current mobility.
3. Follow up in three months for a routine check.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: Residual hemiparesis after an ischemic stroke, right non-dominant side: I69.353 (HCC 253).

distractors.why: Check the documented handedness; when it is not documented, the right side is dominant and the left side non-dominant.
Residual hemiparesis is documented: code the sequela (I69.35-, HCC 253), not Z86.73.
